summary: Stochastic differential equations (SDEs) describe dynamical systems where deterministic flows, governed by a drift function, are superimposed with random fluctuations, dictated by a diffusion function. The accurate estimation (or discovery) of these functions from data is a central problem in machine learning, with wide application across the natural and social sciences. Yet current solutions either rely heavily on prior knowledge of the dynamics or involve intricate training procedures. We introduce FIM-SDE (Foundation Inference Model for SDEs), a pretrained recognition model that delivers accurate in-context (or zero-shot) estimation of the drift and diffusion functions of low-dimensional SDEs, from noisy time series data, and allows rapid finetuning to target datasets. Leveraging concepts from amortized inference and neural operators, we (pre)train FIM-SDE in a supervised fashion to map a large set of noisy, discretely observed SDE paths onto the space of drift and diffusion functions. We demonstrate that FIM-SDE achieves robust in-context function estimation across a wide range of synthetic and real-world processes -- from canonical SDE systems (e.g., double-well dynamics or weakly perturbed Lorenz attractors) to stock price recordings and oil-price and wind-speed fluctuations -- while matching the performance of symbolic, Gaussian process and Neural SDE baselines trained on the target datasets. When finetuned to the target processes, we show that FIM-SDE consistently outperforms all these baselines.
core_methodology: The paper introduces FIM-SDE, a pretrained foundation inference model (leveraging concepts from amortized inference and neural operators) designed to estimate the drift and diffusion functions of Stochastic Differential Equations (SDEs) directly from noisy time series data using in-context (zero-shot) or finetuned estimation. This bypasses complex, per-dataset training procedures.
data_sources: Noisy, discretely observed time series data, including synthetic SDE paths, stock price recordings, oil-price fluctuations, and wind-speed fluctuations.
alpha_potential: The ability to rapidly and accurately infer the underlying drift and diffusion parameters of market processes (like stock prices) from noisy data offers significant potential for high-frequency trading and risk modeling. This methodology could be used to better model market impact, volatility clustering, or complex systemic risks by deriving more robust SDE models in real-time, leading to improved forecasting and optimal execution strategies.
title_cn: 基于基础推理模型的随机微分方程的上下文学习
summary_cn: 该研究提出FIM-SDE模型，能够从嘈杂的时间序列数据中快速、准确地推断随机微分方程（SDE）的漂移和扩散函数。在金融领域，该技术可用于实时估计股价或波动率的潜在动态结构，从而为高频交易和风险管理提供更优化的SDE模型，有望改进市场预测和最优执行策略。

title: phepy: Visual benchmarks and improvements for out-of-distribution detectors
summary: Applying machine learning to increasingly high-dimensional problems with sparse or biased training data increases the risk that a model is used on inputs outside its training domain. For such out-of-distribution (OOD) inputs, the model can no longer make valid predictions, and its error is potentially unbounded. Since testing OOD detection methods on real-world datasets is complicated, we design a benchmark for OOD detection, which includes three novel and easily-visualisable toy examples. These simple examples provide direct and intuitive insight into whether the detector is able to detect (1) linear and (2) non-linear concepts and (3) identify thin in-distribution (ID) subspaces (needles) within high-dimensional spaces (haystacks). We use our benchmark to evaluate the performance of various methods from the literature. Since tactile examples of OOD inputs may benefit OOD detection, we also review several simple methods to synthesise OOD inputs for supervised training. We introduce two improvements, $t$-poking and OOD sample weighting, to make supervised detectors more precise at the ID-OOD boundary. This is especially important when conflicts between real ID and synthetic OOD sample blur the decision boundary. Finally, we provide recommendations for constructing and applying OOD detectors in machine learning.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a benchmark ('phepy') and methods for evaluating and improving Out-of-Distribution (OOD) detection algorithms. This involves analyzing how well detectors identify inputs outside the training domain, specifically using visualizable toy examples to test detection of linear/non-linear concepts and 'needle-in-a-haystack' scenarios. Improvements like 't-poking' and OOD sample weighting are proposed to refine the ID-OOD decision boundary for supervised detectors.
data_sources: The research focuses on benchmark and synthetic toy datasets for OOD detection testing. In a trading context, this methodology would be applied to real financial time-series data or features derived from market activity.
alpha_potential: The core application here is robustness and risk management for ML models deployed in finance. Trading models frequently encounter structural breaks (regime shifts, black swan events) which constitute OOD data. A robust OOD detector allows a system to identify when its predictions are unreliable due to unseen market conditions, enabling it to switch to a safer strategy (e.g., reduce leverage, use a simpler benchmark model, or halt trading). This minimizes catastrophic losses during regime changes, which is crucial for sustaining long-term alpha.
title_cn: phepy：用于分布外检测器的可视化基准和改进
summary_cn: 该论文关注如何识别和应对机器学习模型在金融市场稀疏或有偏数据下的“分布外”（OOD）输入。在量化交易中，这直接关系到模型在市场结构突变时的健壮性。通过引入新的基准和改进方法（如t-poking），该技术可用于构建更可靠的风险控制模块，确保模型能在无法做出有效预测时及时退避，从而减少极端风险敞口，保护策略的长期表现。

title: A Robust $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(1/\sqrt{T})$ Rate for Unprojected TD Learning with Linear Function Approximation
summary: We investigate the finite-time convergence properties of Temporal Difference (TD) learning with linear function approximation, a cornerstone of reinforcement learning. We are interested in the so-called ``robust'' setting, where the convergence guarantee does not depend on the potential function's minimal curvature. While prior work has established convergence guarantees in this setting, these results typically rely on the artificial assumption that each iterate is projected onto a bounded set. Removing such a condition was left as an open problem by Bhandari et al. (COLT'18), hypothesizing the need for additional ``regularity conditions''. In this paper, we show that the simple unprojected TD(0) converges with a rate of $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}\left(\frac{\|\theta^*\|^2_2}{\sqrt{T}}\right)$ in expectation, even in the presence of Markovian noise. We do not require an additional regularity condition, but only a minor polylog correction to the learning rate. Our analysis reveals a novel self-bounding property of the TD updates and exploits it to guarantee bounded iterates.
core_methodology: This paper presents a theoretical convergence analysis for Temporal Difference (TD) learning with linear function approximation under unprojected updates. Specifically, it establishes a robust $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(1/\sqrt{T})$ convergence rate for TD(0) without requiring artificial projection onto a bounded set, resolving an open problem in RL theory.
data_sources: The analysis is based on theoretical Markov Decision Processes (MDPs) used in Reinforcement Learning, typically involving state transitions, rewards, and value functions. In a practical trading context, this methodology would be applied to sequential decision-making tasks using historical market data (prices, volume, order book data) to estimate optimal trading policies.
alpha_potential: The paper develops a robust convergence guarantee for TD learning, a core algorithm in Reinforcement Learning. While the result is theoretical, it provides a solid foundation for applying model-free RL to complex sequential decision-making problems in finance, such as dynamic portfolio management or optimal trade execution. Knowing that the unprojected updates (which are often simpler and more practical to implement than projected ones) converge robustly allows practitioners to deploy these RL agents more confidently in volatile market environments without needing computationally expensive projection steps or strong assumptions on the state space structure.
title_cn: 无投影TD学习在线性函数逼近下的鲁棒 $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(1/\sqrt{T})$ 收敛率
summary_cn: 本文解决了无投影TD(0)学习在金融市场环境下的收敛性问题。研究证明了在不施加人工约束的情况下，TD学习在期望中能达到 $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(1/\sqrt{T})$ 的收敛速度。该理论突破增强了基于强化学习的动态交易策略（如投资组合优化或动态做市）在实际部署中的稳健性，提高了算法在复杂、无界市场状态下的可靠性。

title: VFEM: Visual Feature Empowered Multivariate Time Series Forecasting with Cross-Modal Fusion
summary: Large time series foundation models often adopt channel-independent architectures to handle varying data dimensions, but this design ignores crucial cross-channel dependencies. Meanwhile, existing cross-modal methods predominantly rely on textual modalities, leaving the spatial pattern recognition capabilities of vision models underexplored for time series analysis. To address these limitations, we propose VFEM, a cross-modal forecasting model that leverages pre-trained large vision models (LVMs) to capture complex cross-variable patterns. VFEM transforms multivariate time series into visual representations, enabling LVMs to perceive spatial relationships that are not explicitly modeled by channel-independent models. Through a dual-branch architecture, visual and temporal features are independently extracted and then fused via cross-modal attention, allowing complementary information from both modalities to enhance forecasting. By freezing the LVM and training only 7.45% of the total parameters, VFEM achieves competitive performance on multiple benchmarks, offering a new perspective on multivariate time series forecasting.
core_methodology: VFEM utilizes a dual-branch architecture to process multivariate time series data. It first transforms the series into visual representations, which are then processed by frozen pre-trained Large Vision Models (LVMs) to capture cross-variable spatial patterns. Temporal features are extracted separately. These visual and temporal features are fused using cross-modal attention mechanisms to generate superior forecasts. A key feature is the high parameter efficiency, training only 7.45% of parameters.
data_sources: Multivariate time series data, likely financial or economic indicators, which are converted into visual representations suitable for LVM input.
alpha_potential: The core alpha potential lies in the model's ability to uncover complex, non-linear cross-variable dependencies that standard channel-independent time series models miss. By leveraging the spatial pattern recognition capabilities of LVMs on time-series visualizations, VFEM could potentially generate more accurate multi-step-ahead forecasts for asset prices, volatility, or macroeconomic indicators, which can directly inform factor construction, signal generation, or optimal trade timing. The efficiency (low training overhead) also makes it practical for rapid iteration in a trading environment.
title_cn: VFEM：视觉特征赋能的跨模态融合多元时间序列预测模型
summary_cn: 该模型将多元时间序列转化为图像，利用预训练的大型视觉模型（LVM）捕捉跨变量的空间依赖关系，克服了传统模型中忽略关键交叉依赖的缺陷。通过视觉特征与时间特征的跨模态注意力融合，VFEM能提高预测精度。这为构建基于复杂多因子交互的领先市场信号提供了新的、高效的方法论，有望增强预测的准确性。

title: Projection and Quantisation: A Unifying View of Learning to Hash, from Random Projections to the RAG Era
summary: Approximate nearest neighbour (ANN) search underpins large-scale retrieval, increasingly within the retrieval-augmented generation pipelines that ground large language models, yet the methods that address it have multiplied across communities until they are seldom read as a single field. We argue they form one field with three design choices, and develop the projection-quantisation-organisation (PQO) lens, under which locality-sensitive hashing, learned binary hashing, deep end-to-end hashing, product quantisation, graph-based indexes, and the binary embeddings of modern vector databases are all settings of three coupled questions: where to place the projections, where to place the quantisation thresholds, and how to organise the resulting codes. The projection-then-quantisation reading is established; our contribution is the third, co-equal organisation stage, a demonstration that the three run unbroken from the field's origins to the deep, product-quantisation, graph, and retrieval-augmented eras, and a reproducible measurement that turns the lens from classifying methods to predicting them. The measurement yields three findings. First, memory is won on the quantisation axis: a one-bit code is a thirty-second the size of the float, and a single full-precision re-ranking pass over a short candidate list recovers uncompressed quality in full. Second, the trade-off orderings the lens anticipates recur unchanged as the embedding grows. Third, where supervision is available, an eight-byte code more than doubles the quality of the two-kilobyte float it replaces. We release these measurements as BitBudget, an extensible benchmark with a live leaderboard, recast generative retrieval's "semantic identifiers" as quantisation codes, and identify the open problems that follow as compact codes return to the centre of large-scale retrieval.
core_methodology: The paper unifies diverse Approximate Nearest Neighbor (ANN) search techniques (like Locality-Sensitive Hashing, Product Quantization, and modern learned binary hashing) under the Projection-Quantisation-Organisation (PQO) lens. It focuses on efficiently encoding high-dimensional embeddings into compact codes to speed up similarity search, emphasizing memory efficiency (quantization) and search organization.
data_sources: The paper fundamentally deals with high-dimensional vector embeddings used in retrieval tasks, which in finance often represent complex financial features, alternative data (e.g., news sentiment vectors), or factor exposures generated by upstream ML models (like LLMs or deep learning models).
alpha_potential: The core value is not a direct alpha signal but a crucial infrastructure component for building high-frequency, large-scale ML-driven trading systems. Efficient ANN search is vital for real-time execution of strategies that rely on matching current market states (represented as embeddings) against vast historical datasets or complex lookups (e.g., in RAG for market commentary analysis). By significantly reducing storage and increasing search speed, this methodology enables the practical deployment of context-aware or deep-learning-based trading agents that require rapid similarity lookups.
title_cn: 投影与量化：学习哈希的统一视角，从随机投影到 RAG 时代
summary_cn: 该研究提供了一种统一的框架（PQO）来高效处理高维向量相似性搜索，这是金融AI（如基于嵌入的因子发现或RAG系统）的核心基础设施。通过优化量化和组织方式，该方法能大幅压缩存储并加速实时检索，对于需要快速匹配市场状态到历史模式的高频或复杂AI交易系统具有显著的工程和应用价值。

title: AlphaOPT: Formulating Optimization Programs with Self-Improving LLM Experience Library
summary: Optimization modeling underlies critical decision-making across industries, yet remains difficult to automate: natural-language problem descriptions must be translated into precise mathematical formulations and executable solver code. Existing LLM-based approaches typically rely on brittle prompting or costly retraining, both of which offer limited generalization. Recent work suggests that large models can improve via experience reuse, but how to systematically acquire, refine, and reuse such experience in structurally constrained settings remains unclear. We present \textbf{AlphaOPT}, a self-improving experience library that enables LLMs to learn optimization modeling knowledge from limited supervision, including answer-only feedback without gold-standard programs, annotated reasoning traces, or parameter updates. AlphaOPT operates in a continual two-phase cycle: a \emph{Library Learning} phase that extracts solver-verified, structured insights from failed attempts, and a \emph{Library Evolution} phase that refines the applicability of stored insights based on aggregate evidence across tasks. This design allows the model to accumulate reusable modeling principles, improve transfer across problem instances, and maintain bounded library growth over time. Evaluated on multiple optimization benchmarks, AlphaOPT steadily improves as more training data become available (65\% $\rightarrow$ 72\% from 100 to 300 training items) and outperforms the strongest baseline by 9.1\% and 8.2\% on two out-of-distribution datasets. These results demonstrate that structured experience learning, grounded in solver feedback, provides a practical alternative to retraining for complex reasoning tasks requiring precise formulation and execution. All code and data are available at: https://github.com/Minw913/AlphaOPT.
core_methodology: AlphaOPT introduces a self-improving experience library for Large Language Models (LLMs) to translate natural language optimization problems into precise mathematical formulations and executable solver code. It employs a continuous cycle of 'Library Learning' (extracting structured insights from failed attempts verified by solvers) and 'Library Evolution' (refining the applicability of stored insights based on aggregate evidence). This method bypasses the need for gold-standard programs or costly retraining by leveraging solver feedback for iterative refinement.
data_sources: The paper evaluates AlphaOPT on general optimization benchmarks, not specific financial datasets. However, the methodology is designed to process structured problem descriptions (modeling tasks) that require precise mathematical formulation.
alpha_potential: The direct application is not a trading strategy itself but a crucial enabling technology for developing complex quantitative trading models. In finance, many challenging problems (e.g., portfolio optimization, trade execution scheduling, risk modeling) require transforming high-level goals into precise mathematical programs (like LP, MIP, or Quadratic Programs). AlphaOPT offers a robust way for LLMs to automate the creation of correct, executable model code based on natural language specifications, significantly lowering the barrier to implementing advanced optimization-based trading logic.
title_cn: AlphaOPT：利用自改进LLM经验库构建优化程序
summary_cn: AlphaOPT提供了一种强大的LLM辅助工具，能将量化策略需求（如投资组合优化、交易调度）的自然语言描述转化为精确、可执行的数学优化代码。通过从求解器反馈中学习和积累经验，它提高了复杂优化模型构建的自动化水平和准确性，对开发尖端量化策略具有重要赋能价值。

title: Decomposable Neuro Symbolic Regression
summary: Symbolic regression (SR) models complex systems by discovering mathematical expressions that capture underlying relationships in observed data. However, most SR methods prioritize minimizing prediction error over identifying the governing equations, often producing overly complex or inaccurate expressions. To address this, we present a decomposable SR method that generates interpretable multivariate expressions leveraging transformer models, genetic algorithms (GAs), and genetic programming (GP). In particular, our explainable SR method distills a trained ``opaque'' regression model into mathematical expressions that serve as explanations of its computed function. Our method employs a Multi-Set Transformer to generate multiple univariate symbolic skeletons that characterize how each variable influences the opaque model's response. We then evaluate the generated skeletons' performance using a GA-based approach to select a subset of high-quality candidates before incrementally merging them via a GP-based cascade procedure that preserves their original skeleton structure. The final multivariate skeletons undergo coefficient optimization via a GA. We evaluated our method on problems with controlled and varying degrees of noise, demonstrating lower or comparable interpolation and extrapolation errors compared to two GP-based methods, three neural SR methods, and a hybrid approach. Unlike them, our approach consistently learned expressions that matched the original mathematical structure. Similarly, our method achieved both a high symbolic solution recovery rate and competitive predictive performance relative to benchmark methods on the Feynman dataset.
core_methodology: This method combines Transformer models, Genetic Algorithms (GAs), and Genetic Programming (GP) to perform explainable Symbolic Regression (SR). It first distills an 'opaque' model (likely a complex Neural Network) into interpretable mathematical expressions by generating and refining multivariate symbolic skeletons derived from univariate components.
data_sources: The abstract primarily mentions synthetic physical or mathematical problems (Feynman dataset), implying the primary data source for the current evaluation is structured data suitable for functional discovery, not necessarily raw financial time series data.
alpha_potential: The primary value lies in generating interpretable, closed-form equations from complex or opaque models trained on financial data. In quantitative trading, this is crucial for model risk management, regulatory compliance, and developing robust alpha factors. If an LLM or complex neural network learns a pattern from market data (e.g., non-linear risk factor relationships), this technique could distill that pattern into a transparent, hand-tunable formula, which is more stable and easier to incorporate into traditional factor models or portfolio optimization routines.
title_cn: 可分解的神经符号回归
summary_cn: 该方法利用Transformer、遗传算法和遗传编程，将复杂的'不透明'模型（如神经网络）蒸馏为可解释的数学表达式。在量化交易中，这可以用于发现透明、结构稳健的因子表达式，将深度学习发现的非线性关系转化为可审计、可部署的交易信号或风险敞口模型，助力模型解释性和鲁棒性提升。

title: Differentiable Weightless Controllers: Learning Logic Circuits for Continuous Control
summary: Controlling autonomous systems under real-world conditions often requires policies that can be evaluated with low latency and minimal energy consumption. Unfortunately, these conditions are at odds with the use of high-precision deep neural networks as controllers. In this work, we introduce Differentiable Weightless Controllers (DWCs), a symbolic-differentiable architecture that learns flexible, non-linear, yet highly efficient control policies. DWCs can be trained end-to-end via gradient-based techniques, yet compile directly into FPGA-compatible circuits with few- or even single-clock-cycle latency and nanojoule-level energy cost per action. Across five MuJoCo benchmarks, including high-dimensional Humanoid, DWCs achieve returns competitive with standard deep policies (full-precision or quantized neural networks). Furthermore, DWCs exhibit structurally sparse and interpretable connectivity patterns, enabling direct inspection of which input values influence control decisions.
core_methodology: Introduction of Differentiable Weightless Controllers (DWCs), a symbolic-differentiable architecture that compiles into highly efficient, low-latency hardware (FPGA-compatible circuits). This contrasts with standard high-precision deep neural networks used for control.
data_sources: The paper uses MuJoCo benchmarks for continuous control tasks (e.g., robotics simulation). In finance, this methodology would be applied to high-frequency market data streams or order book dynamics.
alpha_potential: The primary value lies in the execution efficiency and ultra-low latency of the resulting controllers. In high-frequency, market-microstructure dominated strategies (like HFT arbitrage or fast market-making), the ability to deploy inference models directly onto hardware (FPGAs) with single-clock cycle latency offers a decisive competitive edge over software-based deep learning inference, regardless of the model's predictive power.
title_cn: 可微无权重控制器：为连续控制学习逻辑电路
summary_cn: 该研究提出一种名为DWC的新型架构，它能将控制策略编译成极低延迟、低能耗的硬件电路（如FPGA）。对于高频交易和市场微观结构策略，这种将模型直接映射到硬件的能力，可以实现纳秒级的决策速度和极低的执行成本，从而在延迟敏感型交易场景中获得显著优势。

title: SVRG and Beyond via Posterior Correction
summary: Stochastic Variance Reduced Gradient (SVRG) and its variants aim to speed-up training by using gradient corrections. Originally proposed over a decade ago, these methods have never been connected to any Bayesian method at a fundamental level. Here, we fill this gap and derive surprising new connections of SVRG to a recently proposed Bayesian method called `posterior correction'. Our main contribution is to show that SVRG can be recovered as a special case of posterior-correction over isotropic-Gaussian posteriors. Novel extensions of SVRG are automatically obtained by using more flexible exponential-family posteriors. We derive two new such extensions by using Gaussian families: a Newton-like variant with novel Hessian corrections, and an Adam-like extension that scales to large problems. Our work is the first to connect SVRG to Bayes and use it to speed-up training.
core_methodology: The paper fundamentally connects Stochastic Variance Reduced Gradient (SVRG) optimization to Bayesian methods via 'posterior correction'. It derives new, potentially faster, and more robust optimization algorithms (a Newton-like variant and an Adam-like extension) by leveraging flexible exponential-family posteriors to improve standard SVRG training.
data_sources: The paper focuses on optimizing machine learning models (training speed-up). In finance, this applies to training complex models like Neural Networks, Reinforcement Learning agents, or large GNNs used for pricing, risk management, or signal generation, utilizing various financial time-series or structured data.
alpha_potential: This research offers significant practical value by providing superior, potentially faster, and more numerically stable optimization techniques tailored for large-scale machine learning problems prevalent in quantitative finance. Implementing these advanced optimization methods (like the proposed Newton-like or Adam-like extensions) can significantly speed up the training and iteration of complex trading models (e.g., deep reinforcement learning agents or high-dimensional factor models), allowing quants to converge faster to better optimal policies or parameter sets.
title_cn: SVRG及其变体通过后验校正的改进
summary_cn: 该研究将随机方差缩减梯度 (SVRG) 方法与贝叶斯理论深度结合，提出了新的优化技术。在量化交易中，这意味着可以更快、更有效地训练复杂的AI模型，如深度强化学习策略或高维度因子模型，从而加速策略迭代和参数优化，间接提升交易模型的性能和收敛速度。

title: Observation-driven correction of numerical weather prediction for marine winds
summary: Accurate marine wind forecasts are essential for safe navigation, ship routing, and energy operations, yet they remain challenging because observations over the ocean are sparse, heterogeneous, and temporally variable. We present an observation-informed correction approach for global numerical weather prediction (NWP) of marine winds. Rather than forecasting winds directly, we learn local correction patterns by assimilating the latest in-situ observations to adjust the Global Forecast System (GFS) output. We propose ORCA (Observation-informed Real-time Correction with Attention), a transformer-based deep learning architecture that (i) handles irregular and time-varying observation sets through masking and set-based attention mechanisms, (ii) conditions predictions on recent observation--forecast pairs via cross-attention, and (iii) employs cyclical time embeddings and coordinate-aware location representations to enable single-pass inference at arbitrary spatial coordinates. We evaluate ORCA over the Atlantic Ocean using observations from the International Comprehensive Ocean-Atmosphere Data Set (ICOADS) as reference. ORCA reduces GFS 10-meter wind error at all lead times up to 48 hours, achieving 45% improvement at 1-hour lead time and 13% improvement at 48-hour lead time. Spatial analyses reveal the most persistent improvements along coastlines and shipping routes, where observations are most abundant. The tokenized architecture naturally accommodates heterogeneous observing platforms (ships, buoys, tide gauges, and coastal stations) and produces both site-specific predictions and basin-scale gridded products in a single forward pass. These results demonstrate a practical, low-latency post-processing approach that complements NWP by learning to correct systematic forecast errors.
core_methodology: The paper introduces ORCA, a transformer-based deep learning architecture for post-processing Numerical Weather Prediction (NWP) outputs, specifically correcting marine wind forecasts. It uses a novel approach involving masking and set-based attention mechanisms to handle irregular, time-varying observation sets, cross-attention to condition predictions on recent observation-forecast pairs, and cyclical time embeddings for efficient inference. The core idea is to learn local correction patterns by assimilating real-time in-situ observations into existing GFS forecasts.
data_sources: The primary data sources are Global Forecast System (GFS) NWP outputs and real-time, in-situ marine observations from the International Comprehensive Ocean-Atmosphere Data Set (ICOADS), which includes data from ships, buoys, and coastal stations.
alpha_potential: While this paper focuses on marine weather, the methodology has high potential for quantitative trading applications. The core innovation lies in using a transformer model (ORCA) to perform low-latency, high-accuracy post-processing corrections of large-scale forecast models (like GFS) by intelligently assimilating sparse, heterogeneous, real-time localized data. This concept is directly transferable to improving forecasts in finance, such as correcting macroeconomic indicators, commodity production estimates (e.g., oil inventories, natural gas storage), or even proprietary high-frequency market dynamics models where forecast errors are common and local observations arrive irregularly. It represents a structured way to derive better short-term predictions by correcting systematic model biases using real-time, alternative data inputs.
title_cn: 基于观测的海洋风场数值天气预报校正
summary_cn: 该研究提出ORCA模型，利用变压器架构实时修正全球天气预报系统（GFS）的海洋风场预报，通过整合不规则的实时现场观测数据（如船舶、浮标），显著提高了短期预测精度。该方法论可直接应用于金融领域的宏观经济或大宗商品预测模型校正，通过融合异构的实时替代数据源来降低现有大模型预测的系统性误差，从而提供更可靠的短线交易信号。

title: Bellman Residual Minimization for Control: Geometry, Stationarity, and Convergence
summary: Markov decision problems are most commonly solved via dynamic programming. Another approach is Bellman residual minimization, which directly minimizes the squared Bellman residual objective function. However, compared to dynamic programming, this approach has received relatively less attention, mainly because it is often less efficient in practice and can be more difficult to extend to model-free settings such as reinforcement learning. Nonetheless, Bellman residual minimization has several advantages that make it worth investigating, such as more stable convergence with function approximation for value functions. While Bellman residual methods for policy evaluation have been widely studied, methods for policy optimization (control tasks) have been scarcely explored. In this paper, we establish foundational results for the control Bellman residual minimization for policy optimization.
core_methodology: This paper focuses on Bellman Residual Minimization (BRM) as an alternative to traditional dynamic programming for solving Markov Decision Problems (MDPs). Specifically, it establishes foundational results for applying BRM to *policy optimization* (control tasks), moving beyond simpler policy evaluation. A key advantage highlighted is the potential for more stable convergence when using function approximation (e.g., neural networks for value/policy representation) compared to standard dynamic programming methods.
data_sources: The methodology is agnostic to specific data sources, as it pertains to solving control problems defined in MDP frameworks. In a financial context, this would involve market data (prices, volumes) to define state transitions and reward functions, analogous to standard Reinforcement Learning applications.
alpha_potential: The core value lies in offering a potentially more robust and stable optimization method for Reinforcement Learning agents designed for sequential decision-making in finance (e.g., optimal trade execution, dynamic portfolio management, high-frequency market making). If BRM indeed offers superior convergence stability with complex function approximators (deep neural networks), it could enable the training of more reliable trading policies in high-dimensional, noisy financial environments where standard RL methods often struggle with divergence or instability.
title_cn: Bellman残差最小化在控制中的应用：几何、平稳性和收敛性
summary_cn: 该研究探讨了Bellman残差最小化（BRM）在策略优化（控制任务）中的应用，作为解决马尔可夫决策过程（MDP）的替代方法。其优势在于使用函数逼近时可能具有更稳定的收敛性。这为开发更稳健的金融强化学习（RL）交易代理，如算法执行和动态投资组合管理，提供了新的优化工具。

title: Latent Spherical Flow Policy for Reinforcement Learning with Combinatorial Actions
summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) with combinatorial action spaces remains challenging because feasible action sets are exponentially large and governed by complex feasibility constraints, making direct policy parameterization impractical. Existing approaches embed task-specific value functions into constrained optimization programs or learn deterministic structured policies, sacrificing generality and policy expressiveness. We propose a solver-induced \emph{latent spherical flow policy} that brings the expressiveness of modern generative policies to combinatorial RL while guaranteeing feasibility by design. Our method, LSFlow, learns a \emph{stochastic} policy in a compact continuous latent space via spherical flow matching, and delegates feasibility to a combinatorial optimization solver that maps each latent sample to a valid structured action. To improve efficiency, we train the value network directly in the latent space, avoiding repeated solver calls during policy optimization. To address the piecewise-constant and discontinuous value landscape induced by solver-based action selection, we introduce a smoothed Bellman operator that yields stable, well-defined learning targets. Empirically, our approach outperforms state-of-the-art baselines by an average of 20.6\% across a range of challenging combinatorial RL tasks.
core_methodology: The paper introduces LSFlow, a solver-induced latent spherical flow policy for Reinforcement Learning (RL) in environments with combinatorial action spaces. It learns a stochastic policy in a compact continuous latent space using spherical flow matching. A combinatorial optimization solver then maps the latent samples to feasible, structured actions. The method also incorporates a smoothed Bellman operator to handle discontinuous value landscapes arising from solver-based action selection, improving stability during value network training in the latent space.
data_sources: The paper focuses on general combinatorial RL tasks and does not specify financial market data. However, the methodology is applicable to any domain where actions are complex, structured, or constrained, such as portfolio allocation, optimal trade execution scheduling, or dynamic routing problems.
alpha_potential: This methodology has significant potential for quantitative trading applications that involve complex, structured decision-making processes. Specifically, it is highly relevant to dynamic portfolio optimization where actions involve selecting weights or asset combinations subject to complex budget, trading volume, or market impact constraints. By effectively handling large, discrete action spaces (e.g., choosing a specific set of orders or a complex allocation structure), LSFlow could lead to robust, constraint-respecting execution and optimization strategies that outperform standard continuous control methods or simpler discrete approaches.
title_cn: 用于组合动作的强化学习的潜在球面流策略
summary_cn: 该研究提出LSFlow算法，用于解决具有复杂组合动作空间的强化学习问题。该方法通过将策略映射到连续的潜在空间并使用组合优化求解器确保动作可行性，有效处理了传统RL在金融场景中遇到的离散且受限的决策空间（如动态投资组合优化和最优执行）。其稳定的价值学习机制有望提升复杂交易策略的性能。

title: A Graphop Analysis of Graph Neural Networks on Sparse Graphs: Generalization and Universal Approximation
summary: Generalization and approximation capabilities of message passing graph neural networks (MPNNs) are often studied by defining a compact metric on a space of input graphs under which MPNNs are equicontinuous. Such analyses are of two varieties: 1) when the metric space includes graphs of unbounded sizes, the theory is only appropriate for dense graphs, and, 2) when studying sparse graphs, the metric space only includes graphs of uniformly bounded size. In this work, we present a unified approach, defining a compact metric on the space of graphs of all sizes, both sparse and dense, under which MPNNs are equicontinuous. This leads to more powerful universal approximation theorems and generalization bounds than previous works. The theory is based on, and extends, a recent approach to graph limit theory called graphop analysis.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a unified Graphop analysis framework to study the generalization and approximation capabilities of Message Passing Graph Neural Networks (MPNNs) across both sparse and dense graphs of any size. This is achieved by defining a new compact metric space over graphs where MPNNs exhibit equicontinuity, leading to stronger theoretical guarantees.
data_sources: The theoretical framework is generally applicable to any data structured as a graph, which in finance includes relational data like supply chains, inter-company ownership networks, transaction graphs, or market dependency graphs (e.g., relationships between stocks or counterparties).
alpha_potential: The theoretical improvements in generalization and approximation for GNNs operating on sparse/large graphs directly benefit financial applications where relationships are often sparse (e.g., inter-day trading networks). Stronger theoretical guarantees mean that GNN models tailored for complex network data in finance (like predicting default contagion or supply chain risk) will be more robust and reliable for generalizing to unseen market conditions.
title_cn: 稀疏图上图神经网络的图算子分析：泛化与万有逼近
summary_cn: 该研究统一了图神经网络（GNN）在稀疏图和稠密图上的泛化和逼近理论。通过定义新的图度量空间，该方法使得GNN在处理跨越不同规模的金融网络数据（如供应链、资产关联网络）时，具有更强的理论保证和更可靠的泛化能力，有助于构建更稳健的基于图形的市场预测模型。

title: Amortized Predictability-aware Training Framework for Time Series Forecasting and Classification
summary: Time series data are prone to noise in various domains, and training samples may contain low-predictability patterns that deviate from the normal data distribution, leading to training instability or convergence to poor local minima. Therefore, mitigating the adverse effects of low-predictability samples is crucial for time series analysis tasks such as time series forecasting (TSF) and time series classification (TSC). While many deep learning models have achieved promising performance, few consider how to identify and penalize low-predictability samples to improve model performance from the training perspective. To fill this gap, we propose a general Amortized Predictability-aware Training Framework (APTF) for both TSF and TSC. APTF introduces two key designs that enable the model to focus on high-predictability samples while still learning appropriately from low-predictability ones: (i) a Hierarchical Predictability-aware Loss (HPL) that dynamically identifies low-predictability samples and progressively expands their loss penalty as training evolves, and (ii) an amortization model that mitigates predictability estimation errors caused by model bias, further enhancing HPL's effectiveness. The code is available at https://github.com/Meteor-Stars/APTF.
core_methodology: Proposes the Amortized Predictability-aware Training Framework (APTF), which uses a Hierarchical Predictability-aware Loss (HPL) to dynamically identify and appropriately weight low-predictability samples during training, combined with an amortization model to correct estimation errors. This approach aims to stabilize deep learning models against noisy or anomalous time series data.
data_sources: General time series data, which in a trading context would imply high-frequency market data, stock prices, volume, derived indicators, or economic indicators.
alpha_potential: This methodology directly addresses a major weakness in applying deep learning to financial time series: noise and regime shifts. Financial data is notoriously noisy, and periods of low predictability (e.g., sudden market dislocations or true randomness) can destabilize models trained on standard loss functions, leading to poor generalization. By actively down-weighting or adapting the penalty for these bad samples, APTF could lead to more robust models for forecasting (e.g., predicting price movement) or classification (e.g., regime detection), potentially yielding more stable and higher Sharpe ratio signals than standard training methods. Its focus on robustness mitigates overfitting to noise.
title_cn: 针对时间序列预测与分类的摊销可预测性感知训练框架
summary_cn: 该框架通过引入动态识别低可预测性样本并逐步调整其损失惩罚的HPL，以及用于修正预测误差的摊销模型，提高了深度学习模型在处理噪声金融时间序列时的鲁棒性。这有助于开发更稳定、对市场异常和噪音不敏感的预测或分类模型，从而增强量化策略的可靠性。

title: An Alternative Trajectory for Generative AI
summary: The generative artificial intelligence (AI) ecosystem is undergoing rapid transformations that threaten its sustainability. As models transition from research prototypes to high-traffic products, the energetic burden has shifted from one-time training to recurring, unbounded inference. This is exacerbated by reasoning models that inflate compute costs by orders of magnitude per query. The prevailing pursuit of artificial general intelligence through scaling of monolithic models is colliding with hard physical constraints: grid failures, water consumption, and diminishing returns on data scaling. This trajectory yields models with impressive factual recall but struggles in domains requiring in-depth reasoning, possibly due to insufficient abstractions in training data. Current large language models (LLMs) exhibit genuine reasoning depth only in domains like mathematics and coding, where rigorous, pre-existing abstractions provide structural grounding. In other fields, the current approach fails to generalize well. We propose an alternative trajectory based on domain-specific superintelligence (DSS). We argue for first constructing explicit symbolic abstractions (knowledge graphs, ontologies, and formal logic) to underpin synthetic curricula enabling small language models to master domain-specific reasoning without the model collapse problem typical of LLM-based synthetic data methods. Rather than a single generalist giant model, we envision "societies of DSS models": dynamic ecosystems where orchestration agents route tasks to distinct DSS back-ends. This paradigm shift decouples capability from size, enabling intelligence to migrate from energy-intensive data centers to secure, on-device experts. By aligning algorithmic progress with physical constraints, DSS societies move generative AI from an environmental liability to a sustainable force for economic empowerment.
core_methodology: The paper proposes a paradigm shift from large, monolithic generative models to 'Domain-Specific Superintelligence (DSS)' societies. This involves constructing explicit symbolic abstractions (knowledge graphs, ontologies, formal logic) to create synthetic curricula, which are then used to train small language models for deep, domain-specific reasoning. This is contrasted with the current scaling approach that leads to high inference costs and generalization failures outside of structured domains.
data_sources: The immediate focus is on structured knowledge representation (symbolic abstractions) used as synthetic curriculum data to train specialized, smaller models, rather than relying on massive unstructured public data.
alpha_potential: The core potential in finance lies in creating highly efficient, domain-specific reasoning agents grounded in explicit financial knowledge (e.g., regulatory frameworks, complex derivatives pricing models, established economic theories). This approach could lead to robust alpha generation in niches where current LLMs fail due to generalization issues or high operational costs. For instance, specialized DSS models could excel at complex arbitrage identification or regulatory compliance analysis, which requires rigorous, structured reasoning, bypassing the computational and environmental constraints of monolithic models.
title_cn: 生成式人工智能的替代性发展路径
summary_cn: 该研究提议用领域特定超智能（DSS）取代大型通用模型。通过构建知识图谱和本体论等符号抽象，训练小型专业化LLM。这有望在金融领域实现高效、低成本的专业推理，用于复杂的策略生成、套利识别或监管分析，解决当前大模型推理成本高和泛化能力不足的问题。

title: Scalable and Private Federated Learning Using Distributed Differential Privacy and Secure Aggregation
summary: This article presents DDP-SA, a scalable privacy-preserving federated learning framework that jointly leverages client-side local differential privacy (LDP) and full-threshold additive secret sharing (ASS) for secure aggregation. Unlike existing methods that rely solely on differential privacy or on secure multi-party computation (MPC), DDP-SA integrates both techniques to deliver stronger end-to-end privacy guarantees while remaining computationally practical. The framework introduces a two-stage protection mechanism: clients first perturb their local gradients with calibrated Laplace noise, then decompose the noisy gradients into additive secret shares that are distributed across multiple intermediate servers. This design ensures that (i) no single compromised server or communication channel can reveal any information about individual client updates, and (ii) the parameter server reconstructs only the aggregated noisy gradient, never any client-specific contribution. Extensive experiments show that DDP-SA achieves substantially higher model accuracy than standalone LDP while providing stronger privacy protection than MPC-only approaches. The proposed framework scales linearly with the number of participants and offers a practical, privacy-preserving solution for federated learning applications with controllable computational and communication overhead.
core_methodology: The paper introduces DDP-SA, a federated learning framework combining client-side Local Differential Privacy (LDP) via Laplace noise injection and Secure Aggregation (SA) using Additive Secret Sharing (ASS). This two-stage mechanism ensures strong privacy during decentralized model training, as only aggregated, noisy gradients are reconstructed, never individual client data.
data_sources: The primary data source for this framework is decentralized gradient updates or model parameters originating from various client devices or data silos participating in a federated learning task. In a financial context, this could involve distinct trading desks, proprietary quantitative models, or different regulatory jurisdictions generating local trading signals or risk estimates.
alpha_potential: This methodology enables the collaborative training of complex AI models (e.g., Reinforcement Learning agents, advanced risk models, or predictive Transformers) across multiple proprietary datasets without requiring data centralization. This addresses the critical barrier of data silos in quantitative finance, allowing for the development of more robust, generalizable models trained on broader, more diverse institutional data while maintaining stringent data privacy and regulatory compliance. The practical application lies in building superior trading models from decentralized institutional alpha research.
title_cn: 使用分布式差分隐私和安全聚合的可扩展且私有的联邦学习
summary_cn: 该框架DDP-SA解决了金融机构间协同训练AI模型时的数据隐私瓶颈。它通过结合本地差分隐私和安全聚合技术，允许各方在不暴露原始数据或局部梯度的情况下，共同训练更强大的交易模型或风险管理系统。这为构建跨机构、合规的先进量化策略提供了实用且可扩展的技术基础。

title: Securing Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Taxonomy of Attacks, Defenses, and Future Directions
summary: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) extends large language models (LLMs) with external knowledge, but this access path also introduces security risks that existing work often conflates with inherent LLM flaws. We frame secure RAG as securing external knowledge access and organize the literature with SLOT, a taxonomy along four axes: the attack Surface (S) where an adversary acts, the defense Layer (L) that controls the same point, the Objective (O) it breaks following the CIA properties, and the Target (T) it pursues, from a single known query (T1) to target-claim manipulation across a query distribution (T2). Mapping attacks, defenses, remediation, and evaluation onto a six-stage knowledge-access pipeline, we expose two structural mismatches. Finally, we discuss directions for more realistic targets, no-blind-spot and adaptively evaluated defenses, stronger confidentiality, and evaluation for multimodal and agentic RAG. The curated paper list for RAG security is in: https://github.com/TreeAI-Lab/Awesome-RAG-Security.
core_methodology: The paper focuses on developing a taxonomy (SLOT: Surface, Layer, Objective, Target) to rigorously classify and analyze security vulnerabilities specific to Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems. It examines attacks against the external knowledge access path of LLMs, which is crucial for secure implementation.
data_sources: The research focuses on the security architecture of RAG systems, which typically involve external knowledge bases (e.g., financial documents, news feeds, proprietary databases) used to augment LLM responses. The data itself is abstracted to represent potential attack vectors concerning knowledge retrieval.
alpha_potential: While not directly proposing a trading strategy, this research is highly relevant for implementing robust AI/LLM-based trading systems that rely on RAG for contextual awareness (e.g., analyzing complex regulatory filings, interpreting news sentiment from vast proprietary document repositories). Securing these RAG systems against data poisoning, manipulation, or leakage (as described by the SLOT taxonomy) is a prerequisite for deploying any LLM-driven quantitative strategy reliably. High integrity in the retrieved context directly translates to higher confidence in the generated trading signals or risk assessments.
title_cn: 保护检索增强生成（RAG）：攻击、防御和未来方向的分类法
summary_cn: 该论文为确保依赖外部知识的RAG系统（常用于金融文本分析和信号生成）的安全性提供了系统性框架。它通过SLOT分类法细化了针对知识访问的攻击面、防御层和目标，对量化团队部署安全可靠的LLM交易和研究工具至关重要。

title: ML-Guided Primal Heuristics for Mixed Binary Quadratic Programs
summary: Mixed Binary Quadratic Programs (MBQPs) are an important and complex set of problems in combinatorial optimization. As solving large-scale combinatorial optimization problems is challenging, primal heuristics have been developed to quickly identify high-quality solutions within a short amount of time. Recently, a growing body of research has also used machine learning to accelerate solution methods for challenging combinatorial optimization problems. Despite the increasing popularity of these ML-guided methods, a large body of work has focused on Mixed-Integer Linear Programs (MILPs). MBQPs are challenging to solve due to the combinatorial complexity coupled with nonlinearities. This work proposes ML-guided primal heuristics for Mixed Binary Quadratic Programs (MBQPs) by adapting and extending existing work on ML-guided MILP solution prediction to MBQPs. We introduce a new neural network architecture for MBQP solution prediction and a new training data collection procedure. Moreover, we extend existing loss functions in solution prediction and propose to combine contrastive and weighted cross-entropy losses. We evaluate the methods on standard and real-world MBQP benchmarks and show that the developed ML-guided methods significantly outperform existing primal heuristics and state-of-the-art solvers. Furthermore, models trained with our proposed extension with combined losses outperform other ML-based methods adapted from MILPs and improve generalization in cross-regional inference on a real-world wind farm layout optimization problem.
core_methodology: The paper proposes an ML-guided approach, specifically using a novel neural network architecture and combined loss functions (contrastive and weighted cross-entropy), to accelerate the solution of Mixed Binary Quadratic Programs (MBQPs) via primal heuristics. This adapts and extends previous ML techniques from MILP solving to the more complex MBQP domain.
data_sources: The evaluation is conducted on standard and real-world MBQP benchmarks, including a real-world wind farm layout optimization problem. While not directly using market data, the methodology relies on structured optimization problem instances.
alpha_potential: MBQPs are a foundational structure for several complex financial optimization problems, particularly in constrained portfolio selection, trade execution optimization (where order placement involves binary decisions and quadratic costs, e.g., transaction impact), and high-dimensional resource allocation. By significantly speeding up the solving of these complex, non-convex, constrained optimization problems, this research enables the use of faster, higher-quality solutions in real-time or high-frequency decision-making processes where current solvers are too slow. This improved speed and performance translate directly into better execution quality or more optimal portfolios.
title_cn: 面向混合二值二次规划的机器学习引导的原始启发式算法
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种新的机器学习方法，利用神经网络加速求解复杂的混合二值二次规划（MBQP）问题。在量化交易中，MBQP常用于受限投资组合优化和高精度交易执行问题。该方法显著提高了求解速度和解的质量，有望使需要快速求解复杂约束条件的策略（如实时大额订单拆分或高频投资组合再平衡）获得实际性能提升。

title: Population-Aware Imitation Learning in Mean-field Games with Common Noise
summary: Mean Field Games (MFGs) provide a powerful framework for modeling the collective behavior of large populations of interacting agents. In this paper, we address the problem of Imitation Learning (IL) in MFGs subject to common noise, where the population distribution evolves stochastically. This stochasticity compels agents to adopt population-aware policies to respond to aggregate shocks. We formulate two distinct learning objectives: recovering a Nash equilibrium and maximizing performance against an expert population. We investigate two imitation proxies: Behavioral Cloning (BC) and Adversarial (ADV) divergence. We then establish finite-sample error bounds showing that minimizing these proxies effectively controls both the policy's exploitability and its performance gap relative to the expert. Furthermore, we propose a numerical framework using generalized Fictitious Play and Deep Learning to compute expert population-aware policies. Through experiments on three environments we demonstrate that standard population-unaware policies fail to capture the equilibrium dynamics. Our results highlight that learning population-aware policies is crucial to avoid being misled by the randomness inherent in common noise.
core_methodology: The paper applies Mean Field Games (MFGs) combined with Imitation Learning (IL) techniques (Behavioral Cloning and Adversarial divergence) to model population dynamics under common noise. It utilizes generalized Fictitious Play and Deep Learning to compute population-aware policies that react to aggregate stochastic shocks.
data_sources: The methodology is demonstrated on synthetic environments, but the general framework implies application to high-dimensional, interacting agent systems typical in order book modeling, market simulation, or large-scale portfolio management where agent actions influence the overall market state.
alpha_potential: The core value lies in developing robust policies for agents operating in environments characterized by common shocks (e.g., macro news, systemic risk events). In trading, this translates to creating execution or routing algorithms that dynamically adjust strategy based on the inferred collective behavior of other market participants (e.g., large HFT pools or institutional flow). Standard RL/IL methods fail here; population-aware approaches could lead to more resilient strategies during periods of high market correlation or systemic stress.
title_cn: 面向带有共同噪声的平均场博弈中的群体感知模仿学习
summary_cn: 该研究提出了在存在共同噪声的市场模拟中，通过平均场博弈（MFG）和模仿学习（IL）来构建对群体行为敏感的交易策略。它强调了策略必须感知宏观冲击对群体的影响，这对于开发在系统性风险或高波动时期表现稳健的算法交易或流动性管理策略至关重要。

title: Quantifying and Optimizing Simplicity via Polynomial Representations
summary: Deep networks often exhibit a preference for "simple" solutions, and such a simplicity bias is widely believed to play a key role in generalization. Yet a broadly applicable, quantitative measure of simplicity remains elusive. We introduce polynomial representations as a distribution-aware, low-dimensional surrogate for neural functions: we approximate a network's predictive behavior along data-dependent interpolation paths using orthogonal polynomial bases, yielding a compact functional representation. We show that the effective degree of this representation serves as a practical simplicity metric that is predictive of generalization across tasks and architectures, and consistently outperforms existing generalization proxies such as sharpness. Finally, polynomial representations naturally yield a differentiable simplicity regularizer, which consistently improves generalization in image and text classification, fine-tuning contrastive vision-language models, and reinforcement learning.
core_methodology: The paper proposes using polynomial representations (approximated via orthogonal polynomial bases along data-dependent interpolation paths) to create a low-dimensional, distribution-aware surrogate function for complex neural networks. The 'effective degree' of this polynomial serves as a practical, quantitative measure of model simplicity, and this measure is shown to be predictive of generalization performance. Furthermore, simplicity regularization based on this metric is introduced and proven effective.
data_sources: The methodology is demonstrated on standard benchmarks for image classification, text classification, vision-language model fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning. For finance, the required input would be the features/data used to train a predictive financial model (e.g., time-series data, alternative data, or order book features).
alpha_potential: The core value lies in improving the robustness, stability, and generalization of deep learning models used for trading. In quantitative finance, generalization (avoiding overfitting to noise or backward-fitting) is paramount. By quantifying and regularizing model simplicity, high-performing models used for forecasting asset returns, classifying market regimes, or optimizing execution paths are expected to show better out-of-sample performance. A simpler model, as defined by the effective polynomial degree, is likely to capture fundamental economic relationships rather than spurious statistical correlations in noisy financial data, thus providing a robust edge.
title_cn: 量化与优化多项式表征的简洁性
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种通过多项式表征来量化和正则化神经网络简洁性的方法。在金融领域，可用于构建具有更强泛化能力和更低过拟合风险的交易模型。通过惩罚模型复杂度（有效阶数），可以训练出在真实市场数据上表现更稳定的预测因子和投资组合优化器，从而提升策略的长期阿尔法表现。

title: Exploring Autonomous Agentic Data Engineering for Model Specialization
summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong performance on general tasks, while often struggling to adapt to specialized domains without high-quality domain-specific data. Existing LLM-based data curation methods primarily rely on human-designed workflows, leaving it unexamined whether LLMs can autonomously execute an end-to-end data engineering pipeline for model specialization. We formalize Autonomous Agentic Data Engineering, a novel task designed to evaluate LLMs as autonomous data engineers that drive model specialization through end-to-end data curation. We frame data as an optimizable component and study agents that plan, generate, and iteratively optimize training data across multiple domains, guided by post-training performance improvement. Experiments show that autonomous LLM data engineers yield substantial gains, as GPT-5.2 constructs a training curriculum that improves a student model by 57.29%, entirely through iterative, agent-driven data adaptation. By illuminating both potential and bottlenecks, our study establishes autonomous data engineering as a measurable capability and charts a path toward agent-driven model specialization (Code will be released at https://github.com/zjunlp/DataAgent).
core_methodology: The paper introduces 'Autonomous Agentic Data Engineering,' where an LLM (acting as an agent) iteratively plans, generates, and optimizes training data without human intervention, specifically to specialize a smaller 'student' model for domain-specific tasks. The agent measures specialization success via post-training performance improvement.
data_sources: The data sources are synthetic or general-purpose datasets used for training the LLM agent, which then generates specialized training data. In a financial context, this would translate to automatically curating and synthesizing market microdata, news events, or factor definitions to train specialized trading models.
alpha_potential: The core value lies in automating the creation of high-quality, specialized training datasets. For quantitative finance, this means an agent could autonomously identify weak areas in a current trading model (e.g., poor performance during specific volatility regimes or specific market events) and automatically generate the precise adversarial or necessary training examples to refine the model, potentially leading to faster adaptation and skill acquisition beyond standard human-curated feature engineering.
title_cn: 探索自主智能体数据工程以实现模型专业化
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种自主LLM数据工程框架，机器智能体可自动规划、生成和迭代优化训练数据，以使特定模型适应专业领域。在量化交易中，这意味着AI可以自主识别模型弱点，并自动创建所需数据，从而加速交易模型（如特定市场环境下的因子模型）的迭代训练和性能提升，实现高度自动化的模型调优。

title: An Empirical Audit of Input Encoders for Multi-Channel Signal Transformers
summary: Transformers consuming multi-channel scalar signals must embed $C$ simultaneous values into one $d_{\text{model}}$-dimensional vector per time step. We audit eight input encoders -- a shared-scalar baseline, per-channel linear projections, an orthogonality regulariser, a nonlinear MLP, block-partitioned concatenation, channel-independent and channel-as-token architectures, and a projected positional encoding -- on a synthetic benchmark where channel identity is informative and on ETTh1, scored by next-step negative log-likelihood. The headline is practical near-equivalence within a wide "top tier": the standard per-channel linear projection matches every alternative up to small, statistically real but practically modest differences. A direct geometric probe attributes this to a spontaneous orthogonalisation of the per-channel projections: they end up near-orthogonal with no explicit regulariser, letting the standard linear recover channel identity from the summed embedding. Two encoders lose decisively: the shared-scalar baseline collapses for information-theoretic reasons we make explicit, and the channel-independent PatchTST-spirit baseline overfits universally on the synthetic benchmark and underperforms on both. Paired tests resolve two small gaps: projecting the sinusoidal positional encoding through a learned linear layer edges the rest at small $C$ by extending this orthogonality to the positional subspace; a nonlinear MLP stem edges them at the largest $C$, with the gap shrinking under more training data. The practical recommendation: use the standard per-channel linear projection by default; reach for something more elaborate only when the task calls for it.
core_methodology: This paper empirically compares eight different input encoder architectures for feeding multi-channel scalar time series signals into Transformer models. The focus is on how to optimally convert multiple features (channels) at each time step into the model's input embedding space (d_model). Key findings involve the robustness of standard per-channel linear projections due to spontaneous feature orthogonalization, and the shortcomings of shared-scalar and PatchTST-style concatenation methods.
data_sources: The research uses a synthetic benchmark to test channel separability and the ETTh1 dataset, which is a standard multivariate time series dataset (often related to energy load forecasting, but representative of financial time series inputs).
alpha_potential: The high practical relevance lies in improving the foundational data ingestion step for any Transformer-based multivariate time series forecasting model in finance (e.g., predicting asset returns, volatility, or order book dynamics across multiple features like price, volume, and technical indicators). By confirming that standard per-channel linear projection is often sufficient and robust, it guides practitioners away from overly complex and potentially overfit initialization schemes, streamlining the development of robust alpha models based on Transformer architectures.
title_cn: 多通道信号Transformer输入编码器的实证审计
summary_cn: 该研究评估了将多通道金融时间序列数据（如价格、成交量等多因子）输入Transformer模型的八种编码方法。结论是默认采用标准的逐通道线性投影通常是最稳健且实用的选择，可避免不必要的复杂度和过拟合。这直接指导了如何高效、可靠地初始化用于金融预测的Transformer模型的输入层，对构建基于Transformer的多因子预测模型具有直接的工程指导意义。

title: Should Demand Models Incorporate Competitor Prices? Oblivious Learning and Algorithmic Collusion
summary: On a platform with many sellers, should a pricing algorithm explicitly model competitors' prices when learning demand? Classical learning arguments suggest an affirmative answer: ignoring competitors induces model misspecification and inefficiency. In contrast, recent work on algorithmic collusion suggests that strategic obliviousness -- deliberately ignoring competitor prices -- may facilitate collusive outcomes and improve profits. We study this modeling choice in a stylized competitive market with unknown noisy demand, in which multiple sellers repeatedly set prices and estimate demand via iterated least squares, and either incorporate competitors' prices into their demand models (informed) or ignore them (oblivious). We first show that, relative to a monopolist, an oblivious seller in a competitive market must explore more aggressively to compensate for the loss of dynamic competitor information. Building on this insight, we characterize market dynamics when all sellers are oblivious and show that prices converge to the competitive outcome under sufficient exploration, while a continuum of pseudo-equilibria arises when exploration decays. Analyzing the resulting price trajectories, we uncover an excursion phenomenon that gives rise to transient collusive patterns that dissipate as learning progresses. In markets with both oblivious and informed sellers, the informed strictly out-earn the oblivious. Read as a strategy game, the modeling choice has a unique Nash equilibrium: the all-informed market, in which prices converge to the competitive outcome efficiently. Overall, our results indicate that collusive patterns are not robust and are not sustained by oblivious modeling; therefore, incorporating competitor information, together with sufficient price exploration, remains a reliable strategy for sellers in competitive markets.
core_methodology: The paper analyzes the impact of strategic modeling choices (incorporating vs. ignoring competitor prices) in iterative learning environments (iterated least squares) for price optimization under unknown demand. It models market dynamics based on seller 'informedness' or 'obliviousness' and analyzes convergence properties and equilibrium outcomes.
data_sources: Theoretical market simulation data based on stylized competitive models with unknown noisy demand; not based on real market data but models market interaction dynamics.
alpha_potential: The finding that informed sellers (those incorporating competitor information) strictly outperform oblivious sellers provides a strong implication for competitive pricing strategies in algorithmic trading or market making. For high-frequency proprietary trading firms or market makers dealing with similar products, optimizing the inclusion of competitor actions (prices, order flows) in demand/liquidity models is crucial. The paper suggests that maintaining a comprehensive, competitive model is superior to deliberate simplification (obliviousness), which might otherwise lead to transient, unstable 'collusive' patterns that are ultimately inefficient.
title_cn: 需求模型应包含竞争对手价格吗？盲目学习与算法合谋
summary_cn: 该研究评估了定价算法中是否应纳入竞争对手价格的策略选择。结论指出，明智地纳入竞争对手信息的卖家（Informed sellers）表现优于盲目忽略者（Oblivious sellers）。对于量化交易而言，这强调了在设计竞争性定价或做市策略时，必须建立包含对手方信号的稳健需求模型，以实现更有效的市场竞争和利润最大化，而非依赖不稳定的、短暂的合谋模式。

title: Supracompetitive Pricing Under AI Monoculture
summary: When competing sellers delegate pricing to a shared AI model, such as a large language model, correlated recommendations combined with performance-driven updates aggregating seller feedback raise a key question: can standard AI deployment practices inadvertently produce supracompetitive pricing? We develop a stylized duopoly model in which two sellers receive pricing recommendations from a shared AI characterized by two parameters: a propensity parameter capturing the model's tendency to set high prices and an output-fidelity parameter measuring alignment between this tendency and actual outputs, with propensity updated via periodic retraining on observed outcomes. We find that configuring AI models for robustness and reproducibility can lead to supracompetitive pricing via a phase transition. Below a critical output-fidelity threshold, competitive pricing is the unique stable outcome. Above it, the model exhibits bistability: both competitive and supracompetitive pricing are locally stable, with the realized outcome determined by the model's initial propensity. Supracompetitive pricing raises average prices, but occasional low-price recommendations complicate detection. With perfect output fidelity, full price coordination emerges from any interior initial propensity. For finite training batches of size $b$, when the initial propensity lies in the supracompetitive basin, the probability of supracompetitive pricing approaches 1 as $b$ increases, with the region of indeterminate outcomes shrinking at rate $O(1/\sqrt{b})$. Any factor reducing alignment between the model's propensity and sellers' actual pricing, whether through diversifying AI providers, introducing recommendation noise, or reducing seller adherence, pushes the market toward competitive outcomes.
core_methodology: This paper develops a stylized game-theoretic duopoly model to analyze the emergent pricing behavior when competing sellers use a shared AI model for recommendations. The core mechanism revolves around how the AI's propensity (bias toward high prices) and output fidelity (alignment with propensity) interact with seller feedback/retraining, leading to potential phase transitions between competitive and supracompetitive stable outcomes. It focuses on the stability analysis of the shared AI deployment.
data_sources: The model is theoretical, deriving insights from stylized market dynamics rather than empirical financial data. However, the insights apply to scenarios where market participants (sellers) use shared prediction or recommendation systems.
alpha_potential: While not a direct alpha signal generator, this research provides a critical framework for understanding systemic risk and non-competitive behavior in markets increasingly reliant on shared AI infrastructure (e.g., shared LLMs being used for market analysis or client interaction). High practical relevance lies in anticipating shifts in market efficiency or collusion tendencies arising from shared AI dependency. For a quantitative trader, this suggests that if a certain sector relies heavily on a few common AI tools, periods of 'supracompetitive pricing' (or its analogous market inefficiency) may emerge, presenting trading opportunities focused on mean-reversion or exploiting coordinated pricing floors/ceilings.
title_cn: AI单一化背景下的超竞争性定价
summary_cn: 该文通过博弈模型分析了共享AI驱动下市场中可能出现的系统性风险——超竞争性定价。研究发现，高保真度的AI模型可能导致价格协调，形成稳定的高价均衡。这为量化交易者提供了关于市场效率和潜在非竞争性行为的理论洞察，尤其是在高度依赖共享AI工具的行业中，可作为判断宏观市场结构风险的理论基础。

title: Performative Learning Theory
summary: Performative predictions influence the very outcomes they aim to forecast. We study performative predictions that affect a sample (e.g., only existing users of an app) and/or the whole population (e.g., all potential app users). This raises the question of how well models generalize under performativity. For example, how well can we draw insights about new app users based on existing users when both of them react to the app's predictions? We address this question by embedding performative predictions into statistical learning theory. We prove generalization bounds under performative effects on the sample, on the population, and on both. A key intuition behind our proofs is that in the worst case, the population negates predictions, while the sample deceptively fulfills them. We cast such self-negating and self-fulfilling predictions as min-max and min-min risk functionals in Wasserstein space, respectively. Our analysis reveals a fundamental trade-off between performatively changing the world and learning from it: the more a model affects data, the less it can learn from it. Moreover, our analysis results in a surprising insight on how to improve generalization guarantees by retraining on performatively distorted samples. We illustrate our bounds in a case study on prediction-informed assignments of unemployed German residents to job trainings, drawing upon administrative labor market records from 1975 to 2017 in Germany.
core_methodology: The paper introduces Performative Learning Theory, studying how predictive models affect the outcomes they forecast, leading to statistical feedback loops. The core methodology involves embedding these performative effects into statistical learning theory, utilizing concepts like min-max and min-min risk functionals in Wasserstein space to model self-negating and self-fulfilling predictions. It culminates in deriving generalization bounds under performativity and proposing retraining strategies on distorted samples to improve generalization.
data_sources: The abstract cites a case study using administrative labor market records from Germany (1975-2017) for prediction-informed assignments. For trading, this methodology could be applied to predicting market reactions to trading signals, order book dynamics, or large-scale trade executions.
alpha_potential: This framework is highly relevant to understanding *reflexivity* in financial markets, a key concept where predictions and trading actions influence market prices. In high-frequency trading (HFT) or large order execution (e.g., TWAP/VWAP schedules), the execution algorithm itself affects the price discovery process. Understanding and modeling this performative feedback loop (e.g., a strategy that pushes the price in the direction it predicts) is crucial. The theoretical guarantees on generalization under performativity directly address the problem of strategy decay when the market adapts to the strategy's presence. Improving generalization by retraining on performatively distorted samples offers a practical avenue for developing more robust execution algorithms and predictive models that account for their own impact.
title_cn: 溯因学习理论
summary_cn: 该理论研究预测行为如何反过来影响市场结果。在量化交易中，这揭示了策略执行自身对市场动态的反馈效应。通过在统计学习理论框架下建立模型（如Wasserstein空间中的极小极大和极小极小风险泛函），可以分析和校准策略的自我实现或自我否定效应。其核心价值在于为构建更能抵抗自身影响、泛化能力更强的交易和执行算法提供理论基础。

title: ReTabSyn: Realistic Tabular Data Synthesis via Reinforcement Learning
summary: Deep generative models can help with data scarcity and privacy by producing synthetic training data, but they struggle in low-data, imbalanced tabular settings to fully learn the complex data distribution. We argue that striving for the full joint distribution could be overkill; for greater data efficiency, models should prioritize learning the conditional distribution $P(y\mid \bm{X})$, as suggested by recent theoretical analysis. Therefore, we overcome this limitation with \textbf{ReTabSyn}, a \textbf{Re}inforced \textbf{Tab}ular \textbf{Syn}thesis pipeline that provides direct feedback on feature correlation preservation during synthesizer training. This objective encourages the generator to prioritize the most useful predictive signals when training data is limited, thereby strengthening downstream model utility. We empirically fine-tune a language model-based generator using this approach, and across benchmarks with small sample sizes, class imbalance, and distribution shift, ReTabSyn consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines. Moreover, our approach can be readily extended to control various aspects of synthetic tabular data, such as applying expert-specified constraints on generated observations.
core_methodology: ReTabSyn is a Reinforcement Learning (RL)-based pipeline for synthesizing realistic tabular data. It uses an RL framework to train a data generator (like an LLM-based model) by providing direct feedback on preserving feature correlations crucial for predictive tasks, specifically prioritizing the conditional distribution $P(y|X)$ over the full joint distribution, especially in low-data or imbalanced scenarios.
data_sources: The method focuses on generating synthetic tabular data, which in a finance context, simulates structured market data such as tick-by-tick order book data, fundamental data, macroeconomic indicators, or sentiment signals represented in tabular formats.
alpha_potential: The primary practical value lies in robust model training under data constraints. Quantitative strategies often suffer from limited clean data (e.g., rare events, specific market regimes, or private datasets). By synthesizing high-utility, low-data training sets that preserve critical predictive signals (feature correlations), ReTabSyn could improve the generalization and robustness of predictive models for signals like short-term mean reversion, high-frequency alpha signals, or regime-switching strategies, particularly for scarce financial events.
title_cn: ReTabSyn：通过强化学习实现的真实表格数据合成
summary_cn: 该研究提出利用强化学习（RL）合成具有高预测价值的表格金融数据。ReTabSyn通过在生成器训练中引入对特征相关性的直接反馈，优化了在低数据或不平衡市场数据场景下的模型泛化能力。这有助于构建更鲁棒的交易预测模型，尤其是在稀有市场事件或数据受限时，从而增强策略的可靠性和性能。

title: Parameter-Free and Group Conditional Online Conformal Prediction
summary: Uncertainty quantification (UQ) is critical for the deployment of machine learning predictors in real-world scenarios where the data distribution may shift over time (i.e., data may not be exchangeable). Online conformal prediction (OCP) methods address this issue at the expense of either (i) group-wise error control or (ii) learning-rate independent implementation. Group-conditional coverage is essential for fairness across different collections of data points and for providing finer UQ guarantees. Parameter-free optimization is crucial for robustness to adversarial and unknown data shifts. We propose a parameter-free algorithm for group-conditional OCP and demonstrate that it achieves the best group-conditional coverage guarantees. We evaluate our algorithm on synthetic and real-world data, demonstrating that our method not only improves the reliability of existing parameter-free OCP methods but also provides prediction intervals that are comparable in size to well-tuned group-conditional approaches. By unifying group-conditional coverage with parameter-free online algorithms, our work lays a foundation for fair and robust uncertainty quantification in shifting environments.
core_methodology: The paper proposes a novel, parameter-free algorithm for Online Conformal Prediction (OCP) that achieves group-conditional coverage. This method is designed to maintain reliable uncertainty quantification (prediction intervals) even as the underlying data distribution shifts over time (non-exchangeable data), without requiring manual hyperparameter tuning (parameter-free optimization).
